Exclusive: Imagining how Tolkien "might have created" the One Ring sequence was central

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The Rings of Power season 3 has now aired its most dramatic moment yet: the forging of the One Ring. In episode 7, Sauron enters Mount Doom and gives everything he has to create the ultimate weapon in his quest for power in Middle-earth.

Creating the sequence was the culmination of years of work for The Rings of Power showrunners JD Payne and Patrick McKay, and for the episode's director, Stefan Schwartz, bringing it to screen for the first time came with "huge pressure".

"You've got so many massive Rings fans and it's tricky because there's nothing in any of the books that describe how the Ring was created, and we scoured everything to try and glean any little bits and pieces," he tells GamesRadar+. "So really approaching that scene, we had to create a whole bunch of new thoughts."

For Schwartz, a lot of this came down to making sure the sequence was magical, and really represented the world that Tolkien created. One element of that was imagining that the One Ring was created by the vibrations of Fëanor's hammer in Mount Doom, rather than simply being forged.

"I wanted Mount Doom to be a real character and actually to work with him rather than just be a place where he happens to be," he explains. "At [Middle-earth's] very inception, a song was created, and then a little bit of darkness was introduced by the song through one of the characters, and then this song created Middle-earth. That music felt really key, and Tom Bombadil is always singing, it seems key to Tolkien's world. So I wanted the idea of music and vibration to be in there."

Another interesting addition to the sequence is how Sauron ends up giving his life to creating the One Ring, before it brings him back. Schwartz said they wanted to play with the audience a bit here too. "The other key moment for all of us was sacrifice, that Sauron has to basically give up his life in order to create the ring, and then the ring brings back his life," he adds. "That moment of death and utter silence was really important."

The final sequence is undoubtedly the show's most cinematic moment yet, and it's little wonder they wanted to bring it to theaters for a special screening. However, beyond spectacle, it seems that, above all, those involved wanted to do justice to the world that Tolkien created.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

"When you've got such an avid fan base, you want to try and be as true as you can be to the lore," Schwartz sums it up. "And then work within that and try to get elements that feel intuitive and connected to if Tolkien had created it, what he might have created."

The Rings of Power season 3 is available to watch on Prime Video now. Check out out The Rings of Power season 3 review for our full verdict as well as everything you need to know about The Rings of Power season 4.

#3899. Poll: Are You Still Happy To Pay For Online Multiplayer On Xbox Consoles?

I'm not sure paid multiplayer makes sense anymore

Paying for access to online multiplayer has been the norm on Xbox consoles for decades now. It's something we've come to expect as part of playing online with friends and other folk around the world. The general understanding is, if you don't have Xbox Live, you're not playing online.

Eight years ago, I bought a gaming laptop to play Battlefield V on the go, and ever since paying for access to online multiplayer hasn't made much sense to me. It's just not something you do on PC. Sure, games like World of Warcraft and Final Fantasy XIV require additional subscriptions in order to play, but the majority of online games, like BFV, only require you to upfront the retail cost and crack on.

Xbox Play Anywhere is probably where console paywalls really start to look silly. Just a few months ago, I bought Subnautica 2 to play with a friend through the Xbox PC app. I could've opted for Steam, but I wanted to work towards those Xbox cheevos (when they eventually arrive). For a couple of weeks, I'd hop on the PC and dive into alien waters with my mate.

One day, I fancied playing on the big screen in my living room, so I installed Subnautica 2 on my Xbox Series X, booted it up and was prompted to buy a Game Pass subscription just to play the same save file I'd been enjoying for weeks through the Xbox PC app. Like I said, a bit silly.

Time went on, and I'd more or less let this go from my head until I read a report from Windows Central a couple days ago, claiming that Microsoft's upcoming Xbox Helix next-gen console could have plans to kill paywalls for paid multiplayer.

"Sources close to Microsoft's plans tell me Xbox Helix was originally conceived as a true console-PC hybrid with access to Windows PC games and stores such as Steam, alongside another major change: no paywall for online multiplayer."

According to Jez Corden, the original plan for Xbox Helix was to create a console-PC hybrid with access to Steam, potentially spelling the end of Xbox's staple multiplayer charges. It kind of makes sense when you think about it. If you can play your Xbox games across both console and PC, whether through disc-to-digital or Xbox Play Anywhere, it seems like pointless friction to lock multiplayer behind a paywall depending on which device you're playing on.

Back in 2021, changes to Xbox's paid multiplayer requirements allowed players without an active Xbox Live Gold subscription to access multiplayer free-to-play titles such as Fortnite, Call of Duty: Warzone and Apex Legends. And today, Xbox Live Gold isn't even a thing, as it's been absorbed into Xbox Game Pass.

So, even if Xbox Helix's original vision has changed somewhat from what Corden initially reported, it's still not out of the question to suggest that paid multiplayer could eventually become redundant.

Pure Xbox, we'd love to hear what you think about this. Make sure to vote in the poll below and tell us more in the comments section.

#3898. Sony defeat $2.6 billion UK class action lawsuit which argued PlayStation's dominant market position fuels "excessive and unfair" game prices

It's a joyous day for lawyers representing plucky little game and console makers Sony. A UK class action lawsuit which accused the company of using the PlayStation Store's dominant market position to fuel "excessive and unfair" prices for digital games has been dismissed in its entirety by the Competition Appeal Tribunal in London.

As reported by Reuters and The Game Business, the body ruled that the lawsuit - brought by Alex Neill on behalf of folks who bought digital games on PlayStation between August 2016 and February 2026 - failed to establish that Sony had infringed competition law.

The lawsuit claimed that PlayStation's dominant position when it comes to selling digital games on its platforms via the PlayStation Store subjected consumers to "excessive and unfair prices", as a result of terms and a 30% commission fee levied against developers. Neill and co argued owning a PlayStation traps game buyers within a competitionless ecosystem, thereby impacting their ability to seek out a better deal.

It's quite similar to the arguments which have been made against Valve in similar lawsuits concerning the Steam overlords' dominance over the PC game buying space, though a key distinction is that there is some competition on PC via the likes of the Epic store and GOG. How effective some of that competition can be in practice is a different kettle of fish, but the options are there.

In a judgement that could potentially factor into the responses to any similar lawsuits against Valve or other PC storefronts going forwards, the tribunal ruled that Sony compete in a wider ‘systems market’ against Xbox, Nintendo and PC, with PlayStation having no legal duty under competition law to allow third-party stores onto their platform as competition closer to home. The latter the tribunal noted would be expensive, complex and come with potential security ramifications.

As if that wasn't enough, the body ruled that as far as the pricing being unfair went, Neill hadn't proven that Sony’s profit margins were excessive and declared there was no evidence the presence of rival storefronts on PlayStation would've seen prices come down. That's essentially the word NO written in the largest font possible on a sheet of paper the size of a table, then.

Every lawsuit's different, especially when filed in different countries, but if I was one of the other class action suits against Sony or another big game seller on the go at the moment, I'd maybe not be feeling so hot right now. On the other hand, perhaps seeing what the tribunal judged Neill not to have provided suffiencient evidence for might aid those other efforts in formulating their arguments ready to face the scrutiny of government bodies and corporate law-talkers.

#3897. Final Fantasy Resonance Devs Are Somehow Surprised That Fans Still Like Turn-Based Combat

"I expected opinions on it might be divided"

Final Fantasy Resonance was met with high praise when it launched on 22nd October 2026, earning a score of 8/10 from us and a critic average of 85 over on Metacritic.

Despite being an adaptation of a somewhat middling mobile title, Resonance's focus on turn-based combat mixed with the handsome HD-2D visuals made it an instant fan-favourite. The developers, however, seem somehow surprised at the positive reception, believing that opinions would be a bit more divided.

This comes via an interview at Game Spark with producer Keisuke Nakashima, co-producer Miki Kimura, and director Hiroto Furuya (thanks, Automaton), who all feel that Resonance's reception exceeded their expectations.

Nakanishi-san said, “I think the action-oriented and 3D Final Fantasy games are wonderful too, but I was surprised to see just how many people, not only in Japan but overseas as well, are eager for the kind of FF they remember from back in the day, with classic turn-based battles and pixel art.”

Development actually focused on appealing to more old-school fans of the series, with Nakanishi stating that the intended direction was for Resonance to feel almost like a follow-up to Final Fantasy 6. "We figured it was something we ourselves would enjoy, and that there would be players out there who’d feel the same way", he said.

With the series being so heavily focused on 3D visuals and action-oriented gameplay in recent years, the team simply didn't expect Resonance to have such mainstream appeal.

"I thought this was a rather unconventional title, so I expected opinions on it might be divided", said Kimura-san. "I think the fact that a game with such an unusual background has been embraced by so many people is a positive for the industry as a whole, and I’m personally very happy to see it.”

Hopefully the positive reception will lead to more original games being made that focus on turn-based combat and 'retro' visuals. There's clearly a demand for it!

#3896. Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair Gets a PS5 Definitive Edition, Out This December

Playtonic has announced Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair is being treated to a new Definitive Edition on PS5, and it's right around the corner.

The new version launches on 15th December 2026, and anyone who owns a digital PS4 version of the game gets a free upgrade. It appears anyone with a physical copy won't get the upgrade.

On base PS5 and PS5 Pro, the new edition will support a 4K resolution at 120fps, better lighting and ambient occlusion effects, higher-fidelity shadows, and two orchestrated soundtracks. Also, if you don't already own it, the Trowzer's Top Tonic Pack is automatically bundled in with the PS5 version.

One of the best platforming adventures of its generation is back, enhanced for PlayStation 5. Yooka & Laylee return for a full-scale 2.5D adventure, with a 3D Overworld that's an adventure in its own right, levels you can alter to create new ways to play, and Capital B's Impossible Lair waiting to test your skills.

A 2D and top-down side game that accompanies the main Yooka-Laylee game, the Impossible Lair went down really well upon its original launch. It's got an 82 rating on Metacritic, and in our own review, we called it an "improvement" on the original adventure.

Liam grew up with a PlayStation controller in his hands and a love for Metal Gear Solid. Nowadays, he's found playing the latest and greatest PS5 games as well as supporting Derby County. That last detail is his downfall.

#3895. The Rings of Power season 3 ending explained: who dies, what happens to Sauron, and more

Join the GamesRadar community for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.

Everything you need to know about The Rings of Power season 3 ending

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The Rings of Power season 3 ending is a surprising one, as the Dark Lord Sauron's last move of this installment is something you probably weren't expecting.

In episode 7, he finally forged the One Ring, which means his victory was seemingly at hand as Númenor and the Elves gathered to stop him. The main action of the episode, however, is reserved for Gandalf and the Blue Wizard Pallando. Below, we break down all the twists and turns of the episode, so you can get up to speed at a glance.

That means there are spoilers ahead, so turn back now if you're not up to date. For everything you need to know about The Rings of Power season 3 ending, head to the below.

The Rings of Power season 3 ending kicks off with the armies of Númenor and the Elves about to face Sauron's army of Orcs and men in battle. Sauron has the Blue Wizard Pallando on his side, and, of course, the Dark Lord just finished forging the infamous One Ring to Rule Them All.

Yet all is not smooth sailing for Sauron. Gandalf proves impossible to corrupt, even after Sauron tries to trick him with a vision of his old Harfoot pal Nori. Meanwhile, Galadriel introduces Celeborn to Elrond and Gil-galad, and Pharazôn decides to fight Sauron despite the terrifying size of the Dark Lord's army.

Sauron gifts Pallando a ring and makes a reference to the wizard becoming the Witch-king. However, it seems this is not Pallando's fate, as Gandalf is able to slip the ring from Pallando's finger and return his old friend to the light side. Sadly, Pallando is stabbed through the chest – though the wizard is able to survive long enough to help Gandalf get rid of Khamûl. Pallando's death spurs the men from Rhûn to abandon the fight.

Gandalf then encounters Tom Bombadil, who is not tempted by Pallando's ring at all. In fact, he takes it from Gandalf and makes it disappear, then declines Gandalf's offer of his hat. Classic Tom.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

Finally, Theo warns Sauron that their forces are now evenly matched with the opposing side's, and Sauron reads a letter from Pharazôn gloating that Númenor is the "king of men." Bizarrely, Sauron chooses to surrender. While Pharazôn laughs heartily, relishing his victory, Gil-galad, Galadriel, and Elrond are more doubtful. The season ends with Sauron smirking, as his theme music plays ominously in the background.

There is only one significant death in The Rings of Power season 3 finale: Pallando. He is stabbed through the chest by a Nazgnagôl, but he dies redeemed. His death makes the forces of Rhûn abandon the incoming war, which turns the tide in favor of the Elves and Númenor. Also killed in this episode is Khamûl, the Nazgnagôl who snared Pallando to Sauron's side in the first place.

Sauron tells Pallando that he could become "a Witch-king no man can slay." Speculation has been rife about who might become the Witch-king in the show, and this seemed to answer all of those questions… until Pallando dies, anyway. The Witch-king is a dark figure, leader of the Ringwraiths, who is ultimately killed by Eowyn (as seen in The Return of the King). With Pallando ruled out, it once again looks like Theo is the likeliest candidate, especially since he couldn't resist rescuing his ring after Galadriel tried to destroy it in episode 7.

Nori returns thanks to a vision from Sauron, meant to deceive Gandalf into joining his side. However, Gandalf is able to figure out that he's not really seeing his old friend by referencing her brother. Then, the illusion ends. Later in the episode we catch a glimpse of the real Nori, looking up at the sky, as Gandalf brings Pallando back to the light. It seems she's not been taken by Sauron at all, and may return in the upcoming season 4.

Galadriel threw Theo's ring into a pot of molten metal to free him from its influence in episode 7. However, Theo was unable to walk away, still mesmerized by its power. So, we can assume he retrieved the ring and returned to Sauron's service in between episodes.

Tom Bombadil makes Pallando's ring disappear, which so impresses Gandalf he offers the other man his hat (which Tom gracefully declines). Just what he has actually done with the ring is unknown for now, since we know for a fact that Sauron will eventually have all nine rings in his power to give to his Ringwraiths.

Since the beginning of the series, there have been ominous signs that Númenor is doomed (as it is in Tolkien's source material). When Sauron surrenders, Pharazôn gloats, while Gil-galad says he sees the "doom of men" in the action. In Tolkien's works, Númenor is essentially destroyed as a punishment for hubris, when it invades the Undying Lands, AKA Valinor, to try and take immortality. Pharazôn is certainly showing this kind of doomed arrogance, which Sauron seems to be taking advantage of – indeed, in Tolkien, Sauron manipulates Pharazôn as his prisoner, and it looks like this storyline is coming in season 4, judging by that smirk.

Sauron receives a letter from Pharazôn gloating that Númenor is the "king of men." It seems the Dark Lord sees some opportunity here, as he immediately goes to surrender to the forces of Númenor and the Elves. While the Elves are wary, Pharazôn is delighted. However, in Tolkien's works, Sauron helps bring about the end of Númenor by manipulating Pharazôn as his prisoner. It looks like this is Sauron's next scheme, signalled by his devious smirk.

Before surrendering, Sauron takes off the One Ring. However, he has most likely concealed it somewhere he can wear it again when he needs it, since we know from Tolkien's work this is not the end of the Dark Lord.

Yes, Amazon has officially announced that there will be a The Rings of Power season 4. The series is in pre-production now and will begin filming in the UK in spring.

No, there is no Rings of Power season 3 post-credits scene. Once the episode ends, you're free to turn it off.

All episodes of The Rings of Power season 3 are streaming on Prime Video now. For more, check out our The Rings of Power season 3 review.

#3894. Only two days out from GTA 6, its publisher Take-Two lay off staff at XCOM and Civilization developer Firaxis

About a third of the workforce has been cut, reportedly

Upsettingly, it is that time of the week again, as Take-Two are laying off staff at Firaxis, the developer behind Civilization and XCOM, only a little over a year the last time the studio suffered from layoffs. Firaxis are, notably, owned by Take-Two, the publisher of GTA 6 which comes out in, oh, two days time? Interesting timing, 'ey.

Word of the layoffs came from Bloomberg, who report that about 60 people are losing their jobs, apparently roughly a third of its staff. The studio's head, Heather Hazen, is also leaving. A spokesperson for 2K Games (the Take-Two label that manages Firaxis) shared a statement on the layoffs: "Firaxis is restructuring and recentering around the studio’s core strength - designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years.

"As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis. These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis." I don't feel personally confident in the idea that the only way to make a company succeed is by laying a bunch of people off thereby making it much harder to make anything in the first place, especially in the lead-up to what will likely be the best selling game of the decade, but what do I know!

Bloomberg also report Firaxis have been working on a new XCOM, which is yet to be announced, but the project has apparently had to contend with numerous development issues, missing a "significant milestone over the summer." This new XCOM game hasn't been cancelled at the very least, but anonymous sources that spoke with Bloomberg said it may have to deal with a shakeup due to the cuts. As always, solidarity with all those affected by this situation.

#3893. GTA 6 Appears To Be Causing Issues On A Small Number Of Xbox (& PS5) Consoles

FWIW, it seems to be happening more on PS5

Over the last few days, I've been running into various bits of discussion on social media about how GTA 6 is crashing or even "frying" some people's consoles, and for the most part it's been talked about in regards to the PS5 version.

This particular clip has been getting a ton of attention this week (profanity warning):

The Verge editor Tom Warren ended up picking up on this, suggesting that "GTA 6 is really stress testing the GPUs inside consoles", and then pointing out that the Xbox Support Reddit community highlights issues on Xbox as well.

And after visiting it, yeah... there's no doubt it's got multiple reports from people who claim GTA 6 has been responsible for either crashing their console or putting stress on the GPU and causing the visuals to stop functioning properly.

Here are just a few examples of people confirming their issues:

Now, as scary as this might seem, it's worth keeping in mind that you're unlikely to run into any major issues. The majority of GTA 6 players are enjoying the game just fine on their Xbox Series X, Xbox Series S and PS5 consoles right now, and I'm willing to bet most people haven't had a single crash whatsoever.

It also should be noted that Rockstar aimed to reduce crashes in their latest update for GTA 6 this week.

News GTA 6 Update Now Live On Xbox Series X|S, Includes Seven Official Fixes

Update: We've got the deets from Rockstar

At the same time, it's also impossible to say how widespread the problem is, but most people speculate that it's limited to anywhere between 0.1% and 5% of Xbox players at most. GTA 6 is an incredibly demanding game without a doubt, and it might unfortunately be exposing some weaknesses in certain consoles for whatever reason.

That's why we're only saying "a small number of" consoles in the headline here, because we don't want you to get scared off from playing GTA 6 over the next few weeks and months. Just keep in mind that it's a good idea to ensure your console isn't too clogged up with dust every now and again, and hopefully you'll never run into issues like this.

#3891. What would Rockstar have done if GTA hadn't taken off? Former tech director Obbe Vermeij on Scottish zombies, James Bond and the "curse" of success

"We ended up just cutting and cutting it."

It's bizarre today to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't Grand Theft Auto. Frankly, it's bizarre to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't GTA 6, which rolls onto console hard drives this week. A decade in the making, with a development team of thousands scattered across an international network of studios, GTA 6 aims to be the Maximum Game. It's both a dense, lively open world and a monument to the exhausting impersonality of "triple-A" game productions. It contains multitudes: birdlife! Realistic cloud formation! Fuel mechanics! Romance! Soda visibly sloshing around in bottles! It's an imperial production shadowed by labour disputes, that appears to have given Rockstar's various teams little time or space to think about anything else.

It wasn't ever thus. Once upon a time, Rockstar weren't just known for GTA and to a considerably lesser extent, Red Dead Redemption. Once upon a time, they had a reputation for slightly dodgy experiments. I recently interviewed former Rockstar North tech director Obbe Vermeij about a few of them, including Agent, the unofficial James Bond game Rockstar toyed with before putting all chips on Grand Theft Auto 5.

During the noughties especially, when the most expensive games took considerably less time to make, Rockstar tried their hand at a number of projects besides GTA. There was 2002's Manhunt, a rancid parody of snuff films – not much loved, but sufficiently admired to spawn a sequel in the hands of Rockstar London. There was 2005's adaptation of Walter Hill flick The Warriors - a mouthy Homeric beat 'em up in which you cross New York on foot over the course of a single night - and 2006's Rockstar Presents Table Tennis - an inexplicable pivot towards realistic sports simulation from Rockstar San Diego. Later in 2006 came Bully, aka Canis Canem Edit, a boarding school life sim from Rockstar Vancouver (née Barking Dog Studios). I didn't warm to Bully, myself, but I've never been able to get its sardonic OST out of my head.

In amongst all these, Rockstar weighed up several game projects that never made it out of the building. The aforesaid Agent is perhaps the best-known, but my conversation with Vermeij (who worked at Rockstar from 1995 to 2009) began with "Z", a fleeting attempt to expand into the world of zombie action games, which Rockstar spent a few weeks mulling over in the wake of Grand Theft Auto: Vice City. It was set in the islands of Scotland, which would have made it the only Rockstar North project to unfold in the studio's backyard. "I think it was meant to be smaller than GTA, map-wise, and there weren't going to be any deserted cities - it was really just islands and some villages," Vermeij told me. "But it really didn't get that far."

The pitch for Z couldn't be further from the sweat and glitter of GTA 6's Miami, but the two projects would have shared a taste for 'simulation' elements. "It actually was going to have cars running out of fuel," Vermeij told me. "That was going to be one of the things, and the whole idea was that you'd find cars and they'd only have a little bit of fuel in them." As for why Z never entered full development, turns out desolate North Atlantic archipelagos full of corpses can be a bit of a downer. "Everybody was super excited to do something new," Vermeij went on. "And then pretty quickly, we kind of realised that it's really just a depressing version of GTA, and it sort of died."

The increasing success of Grand Theft Auto during these years was something of a "curse", Vermeij went on. It meant that a lot of Rockstar's ventures beyond GTA were eventually folded back into the series. "It's very difficult to have a studio and have one mega game, and then do something on the side," he explained. "It's almost impossible, because at any time during the development of the smaller project, management's going to say 'oh! The big project's in trouble. We need more people.' And they're just going to pull everybody from that small team onto the big team, so even if we had progressed with [Z], what would have happened is we would have had to start GTA 4 at the same time, and eventually the small team would just be merged with the big team again."

Rockstar's Bondalike game Agent got a lot further down the road to release than Z. It was in development for several years following GTA 4's launch, and was touted by co-founder Sam Houser as Rockstar's next megagame. "A lot of work had been done on that," Vermeij recalled. "And then we ended up just cutting and cutting it, because the same thing happened – at some point you kind of go OK, well, we better get on with the next GTA."

Agent sounds like it could have been a hoot, at least going by Vermeij's description of his own time with the project. It was a relatively linear, level-based action game with a touch of camp. "There was a French ski resort, and there was going to be a Mediterranean town like San Tropez, somewhere like that," Vermeij explained. "There was going to be a North African place, like Morocco or Egypt. The last level was going to be on the moon, with lasers – like Moonraker. There was another one, London or something, I can't remember. But then we just ended up cutting everything down, because what we could see happening was that at some point, we would have to go back to work on GTA. It wasn't close to being finished."

While never a spoof in the vein of Austin Powers, Agent would have been a sillier production than the grimy and downbeat GTA 4. "It was meant to lean into all the cliches," Vermeij said. "It was like James Bond from the 1970s - there was a girl with white boots. It wasn't a comedy, it was just completely over-the-top cliched."

As for the choice of a level-based format, this came from a desire for variety the studio couldn't realistically achieve in a GTA-style open world. "If you had to have them all on one map, you would basically have had to model a mini version of Europe," Vermeij said, "So you couldn't do that." Players might have been able to revisit locations containing several missions, which calls to mind Io Interactive's later Hitman: World of Assassination games, to say nothing of their own bash at the Flemingverse, 007 First Light. "I don't how whether it was going to be completely linear, or whether you were always going to be able to visit all those locations." Vermeij said.

Needless to say, Rockstar's Bondalike would have featured chase scenes. Vermeij himself worked on the moving parts. "I remember doing some work on what we called the car recording stuff for GTA," he went on. "So if a level designer wanted to set up a chase scene, they would drive one car, record it, and then play back the recording, drive a second car and record that... and so driving one by one, you could set up a whole chase scene. I did a version of that for [human] characters as well, because for one of the Agent missions in the French ski resort, there was like a chase where the bad guys were on skiis and using their machine guns. So I set up a thing where you'd play them one by one, and then play the whole thing back. There was maybe like five or six bad guys and they'd ski after you, and then it was just up to the player to avoid them."

According to Vermeij, Agent never had a defined story during his time with it. It was more of a mix of scenario concepts, "kind of how we used to do games with GTA 3 and Vice City". Mind you, the absence of a nailed-down plot isn't necessarily a sign that Agent was lightyears from being finished. Even at their most byzantine, Bond movie plotlines often feel like an afterthought. "It's like oh yeah, there's a bad guy and there's a thingally-dingally that needs to be captured before the world comes to an end," summarised Vermeij. Still, Agent would spend a long time in limbo after Vermeij left. It's still unclear how much it was in active development before Rockstar's trademark finally evaporated in November 2018.

One thing I learned while reading up on Rockstar's checkered history was that GTA 3, the game that made GTA a Thing on PlayStation, wasn't deemed an immediate hit at launch. According to Vermeij himself, it was months before Rockstar realised what they'd built. This inspired an obvious closing question: what might Rockstar have done, if GTA 3 hadn't blown up the way it did? Which of those other projects might have become the focus?

"I really have never thought about it," Vermeij pondered. "When Rockstar San Diego joined, it was 2002, and they already had a bunch of games and a bunch of franchises, like Midnight Club and Smuggler's Run. They were already into driving games and city games in that way, so it wouldn't have surprised me if we'd gone in that direction anyway. But then they were more about car modding and decals and stuff like that.

"At Rockstar North, we only had Manhunt and GTA," he went on. "With Manhunt, that team was in development hell for a while, they had a couple of rough years where they got stuck and in the end, they pulled through, and they got a pretty decent game. But I don't think that would have been the future. I don't think [Rockstar North] would have done a Manhunt 2. So yeah, it would be Table Tennis, I think! Everything on Table Tennis!"

With no discounts on the official Nintendo Switch 2 Pro Controller in sight, it's worth weighing up whether that $89 price tag is worth it after all.

Here's what the Nintendo does that others... Nintendon't.

The Switch 2 Pro Controller is unmatched in its ability to wake the Switch 2. Others can, and will, bring that screen to life in docked mode, but setup is finnicky and dropouts are regular. The Switch 2 talks to its own gamepad best.

You also won't find Nintendo-specific HD Rumble 2 haptics in third party alternatives. That's the more nuanced level of vibration that makes games like Donkey Kong Bananza sing just that little bit brighter. Haptics are available in third parties, but without that Ninty spark.

Finally, onscreen control over your back button assignments is exclusive to Nintendo's gamepad. Being able to quickly pause your game and configure each of the two additional clickers is super handy - others will have you connecting to a PC or mobile app, or working out individual button presses on the gamepad itself.

If any of those are deal breakers, the Switch 2 Pro Controller is worth it. If you can live without those luxuries, though, third parties have plenty to bring to the table. GameSir and 8BitDo add trigger stops, Hall effect thumbsticks, charging docks, and extra configurable buttons to the party, for example.

What do you get for your money? Quite a lot.

The Super Nova feels far more premium than that $30 price tag would suggest. While alternatives like the PowerA Advantage Wired Controller can undercut it by around $10 when the discounts are flowing, they also feel light, hollow, and creaky in the hands. This is as solid as it gets, with nicely rubberized grips, satisfying buttons, and a premium heft.

Customization is your main point of value in this price. Back buttons are par for the course these days, and trigger-stops are creeping down the price scale as well, but motion controls can also be mapped to mouse inputs on PC, GameSir's Connect software can change everything from stick deadzones to trajectory settings, and - of course - that RGB is configurable as well.

Is it perfect? No. I scored the GameSir Super Nova 4/5 stars in my review, dropping points for its lack of presets, rigid-feeling d-pad, and finnicky wake functionality. The latter is a particularly sore point. It was one of the biggest reasons I was so excited to wrap my hands around this gamepad, but in all my testing I just never got it to work. It's a fairly convoluted setup process anyway, but others have been able to get everything running smoothly.

Ultimately, paying more for the GameSir Super Nova over budget gamepads from PowerA and PDP is a no-brainer in my experience.

#3889. Archetype go all in on the Mass Effect vibes with a FemJun reveal, but I'm just left hoping they'll call the alternative option MascJun to balance it out

I know it, you know it, hell, I'm sure developer Archetype Entertainment know it: Exodus is kind of just Mass Effect again. That's in part because the DNA of the game has been built by series vets like Drew Karpyshyn, Chad Robertson and James Ohlen. But it's also because, well, they're putting FemShep in the game. Yes, I'm being a tad facetious here, but when the latest trailer for your game is literally titled "Female Jun Reveal," well, comparisons will be made!

To top it all off, a blog post from the devs literally refers to the alternate gender for the protag as FemJun. They know what they're doing. In any case, first up, her voice actor! She's being played by Carina Conti, an up and comer last digitally heard in Mafia: The Old Country as Isabella Torrisi. Male Jun (who hasn't been given a nickname, which couldn't possibly serve to other female Jun (and MascJun is right there!)) has also had his voice actor confirmed as Stephen Oyoung, who you'll have heard as Mister Negative in Insomniac's Spider-Man games and Red Hood in Gotham Knights.

It's been previously confirmed that no matter which gender you pick for Jun, you'll be able to romance whoever you like, so, happy smoochin'! The story will stay the same too, as will dialogue options, though I'm imagine some pronoun switcheroos will take place somewhere along the line.

I'm mostly just left feeling that this doesn't really seem like it'll fix the game's boring hero problem. Edwin made note of Jun's quite lacklustre vibe earlier this year, aptly tearing down MascJun's Instagram visage, though this was prior to the face model and voice actor change the character has undergone. Personally, I'm not sure that'll be enough, and FemJun kind of matches that Instagram look; the perfect bun and bangs that pop out when she takes her helmet off is quite silly too. Ah well! A game isn't done until it's done (which, in theory, will be April 7th next year).

I've been lucky enough to test controllers, headsets, and all sorts of technology for a living during all that time, so I'm all about building that dream setup with the best gear and helping you to do just that. I've also been covering the RAMpocalypse closely this year, so I'm determined to beat all the expensive doom and gloom of shopping for technology right now. If that sounds up your street, come along for the ride.

After seeing price hikes this year, it's not a nice time to be shopping for a PS5 console. For that reason, I'd say going with a refurbished model is actually the best option. It may not be ideal, but PlayStation's own refurbished models are properly certified before they're resold, so you probably won't even notice that it's not brand new. Moreover, you're much closer to the launch price for the console if you go for a pre-owned model - even if it should be a lot cheaper than it was at launch at this point in its life.

The DualSense Edge hardly ever gets discounted, and I think the only reason it is at the moment is because of GTA 6's monumental launch. I'd recommend this Black Friday PS5 deal because we seldom see it for cheaper. The opportunity comes so infrequently it's just got to be one you consider - even if there are other third-party PS5 controllers I'd recommend to those who want more functionality.

The Fractal Scape isn't a headset you'll see recommended super often compared to SteelSeries, Razer, and these brands that are synonymous with PS5 and Xbox audio. This is the headset I use on a daily basis, and it's stupidly good for the money. Comfortable, well-designed, excellent audio quality, a classy charging stand, and multi-platform compatibility. Can strongly recommend this Black Friday PS5 deal.

Saros, the spiritual successor to Housemarque's Returnal, arrived on the shelves earlier this year, and didn't quite have the same impact as some of the other big-name PS5 franchises Sony has in its roster. For that reason, you may have been waiting for a discount, or for a gap in your gaming schedule before getting it. When a brand-new Sony AAA, PS5 exclusive is $40 within a year of its release, it's hard not to argue it's a good deal.

Similarly to Saros, Wolverine is even newer and is also seeing a discount at the moment as a part of Black Friday PS5 deals. Again, this wasn't the best-received game of 2026 (maybe due in part to Sony's ending of physical media support), but it's one of the PS5's biggest titles and hotly anticipated games, so it's hard not to argue that this is a deal you should know about. How often do we see first-party PS5 exclusives discounted two months after launch?

GTA 6 launched alongside two DualSense controllers, but neither the limited edition black model nor the special edition white model are discounted this Black Friday. There are still plenty of different colorways and editions available for $20 off across the web right now, but anyone holding out for those palm tree vibes will need to wait a little longer.

Rather bizarrely, I couldn't seem to find the Scuf Omega (the brand's latest PS5 controller) at Amazon in the UK earlier on, when there's been healthy stock since launch. It's now back again, but at full price, and in the US, it's still sitting at $219.99.

Maybe a sudden deal will hit later in the week? It's a bit strange that Scuf isn't throwing down the gauntlet when Razer and Nacon both are.

More on this story as it develops, but it's hard to recommend the most expensive PS5 controller while it's at full price and the others are getting discounts.

I'm still perusing the shelves at PlayStation Direct (yes, perusing).

I've just found that the Certified Refurbished DualSense Edge is in the Black Friday sale. Given the DualSense Edge has been given a discount at every retailer, surely that means a pre-owned one is even cheaper, right?

The Certified Refurb costs $144 at the moment, which is only $25 cheaper than the brand-new version you can get in either color at any other retailer.

I trust Sony's certified refurb ratings, but with the DualSense Edge, a controller that's prone to stick drift and other durability problems, I maybe wouldn't take the risk.

If you're looking for an even cheaper way to get a DualSense Edge at the moment, though, you might want to give this a look.

Certified Refurbished DualSense Edge: $169 $144 at PlayStation

PlayStation Direct actually has a Black Friday sale, and it's not terrible, and hey, at least you know there's official gear here you're not going to see falsified prices for?

On bundles, things are pretty thin, although I did notice that the certified refurbished bundle for the Slim, Physical edition along with a bundled Midnight Black DualSense is "coming soon" - so maybe that's something for us to keep our eyes on.

I'm not massively convinced that this falls under this banner, but in a lot of cases, retailers of hardware brands can hold stock back until the actual Black Friday day itself, then release it. So sometimes you do get these somewhat false "early stock issues" happening in the days before it.

This is a refurbished model though, so it's far more likely we're seeing a lack of stock due to more units being bought at the moment, and fewer being returned. Thanks, Rockstar.

Either way, maybe this is one to keep an eye on in the coming days.

PlayStation 5 Slim Physical Edition + Midnight Black DualSense: $549 at PlayStation Direct

Which, of course, means none of them are available. At least here, the bundles that are coming up in search results feel official.

They're bundled in packaging straight from Sony and are relatively simple, with a game or two along with the console.

But all of them, from God of War Ragnarok to Spider-Man 2, NBA 2K26, and MWII, are all unavailable. Apparently, we can't have nice things this Black Friday.

Okay, it hasn't gotten much better after scrolling through these PS5 bundles.

Almost all of these are over a grand, which doesn't match up at all with the price of the hardware included in the bundles, so they're just not worth recommending.

I had hope for a second, because this Wolverine bundle costs $689.98 at Best Buy. You get a Slim Physical Edition of the console and a copy of Wolverine - and even a saving of $30.

I just switched over to Best Buy to compare and what do you know, that exact same GTA + accessories bundle is available here too, but for even more money.

That's one I'd definitely steer clear of, folks.

And I'm not going to lie, it's slim pickings. These are the findings I'm seeing from a quick search.

The majority of these listings are out of stock, and many of them feel like obsolete bundles that aren't even offered anymore, like the Ghost of Yotei Gold Edition, for example. Meanwhile, the Wolverine version of the console is $924, which is hard to recommend even if you do get a rare cosmetic version of the PS5 and a few extras.

Yes, there are lots of listings, but so many of them are over $1,000, which just isn't worth the price you're paying - even with the RAMpocalypse driving prices up. You could get a more powerful gaming PC to play on for that kind of money, and I'm never convinced all of Walmart's online offerings are legit. The key while shopping for a PS5 right now is to stick as closely to MSRP as possible.

Maybe I'll drop a post in a while with those official MSRPs in the UK and US just so you actually know the guidelines to stick to.

Truth be told, the only option I'd really consider recommending from Walmart is this GTA 6 and Accessories kit. I'll warn you and say the accessories look very questionable and are not made by brands we've tested and tried. In the bundle, you get a PS5 Slim Physical console, GTA 6, ~a headset~, controller wrap, extra cables, what looks like a box stand for displaying physical games, and a controller stand.

All that, and it's $929, which is pretty hard to quantify because none of these accessories are named brands we can see sold separately.

This is what I mean: Walmart's bundles feel questionable, so I'm going to rate this one with a hesitant "maybe look elsewhere".

Alright, just in case you're on the hunt for a console, I'm going to go take a quick look around the retailers and see what each one is offering in terms of bundles and availability. Spoilers, there probably won't be very many good ones based on what I've seen so far.

I'm going to try and find PS5 consoles on sale that offer a little extra, don't cost way too much money, and are readily available to actually buy right now.

I'm hunting high and low for a cheaper way to recommend you get GTA 6 if you haven't already, but it's just not happening. In the last few days, I did find a $75 PSN voucher for $70 at Newegg which might have helped somewhat toward the cost of buying the game digitally, but the shelves are just too volatile at the moment and it's gone.

If you want to buy the code in the box, Amazon still has stock, but it's sadly at full price.

Reminder that if you're in the UK, you can still make the most of that discounted PSN voucher at ShopTo, linked below.

Hell is Us is on sale, and that's a game I'd highly recommend from last year. Annoyingly, it's not seeing the deepest discount in the world at the moment, especially compared to some titles that dropped this year, but it's a really solid game I enjoyed playing a lot. If you're in the UK, it's a very, very reasonable price.

You play as a relatively normal guy trying to rediscover his origins after he learns that his parents sent him away from his home country as a child. Only one problem: there's a civil war going on when you return, and a lot of what look like demons roaming the countryside and killing everyone make everything a whole lot worse.

The best way I can describe Hell is Us is by saying it's like Assassin's Creed if the game design matured to a point of almost 90s retro-nostalgia? There's very little hand-holding, a lot of clever threads to follow, and combat that feels great. It also isn't a soulslike, which I celebrate hard.

It's discounted at Amazon now, and if you're looking for something else to play, check it out.

They're surprisingly difficult to find this Black Friday, and even pre-owned/open box/refurbished ones are sold out (presumably because nobody in their right mind wants to pay today's current price for Sony's console, and GTA has caused a big boost in sales lately).

But, Walmart is listing the Slim Digital Edition PS5 at its official price. I'd still recommend the certified refurbished model if you can get it at PlayStation Direct, but I'm just trying to give you as many options as possible.

There are plenty of colorways of the DualSense, and pretty much all of them are going a little cheaper this week. If you're not so interested in the extra buttons and swappable parts of pro controllers, Black Friday PS5 deals might just be the best way for you to expand your collection of stock DualSenses.

There are even limited edition colorways that are a bit cheaper at Amazon than their launch price, so it's worth a look. That doesn't include some of the latest ones though. The new Prism collection isn't on sale, for example, but a lot of the various colorful ones are.

As promised, here's another PS5 game deal that folks in the US can actually make the most of.

AC Black Flag Resynced is another example of a 2026 release that's already seeing a discount in this year's Black Friday PS5 deals.

If you want to experience the remaster of Kenway's big Caribbean adventure, you can do so now for a lower price.

Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced: $30 at Amazon

Okay, so there's no UK equivalent of this one. It's impossible to please everyone, I guess.

Read more: Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced review

Mortal Shell 2 is also seeing a really sweet discount in the UK. Annoyingly, there's no US equivalent for this one, so I apologise for that. But this deal is too good not to recommend to the UK readers.

I'll be back in a second with a US game deal, I promise.

I've found two games from 2026 both seeing great discounts at the moment. Both have been reviewed really well, but have flown a little under the radar considering some bigger titles dropping in the same year.

The first is Star Wars Zero Company, which will be a big hit for anyone who enjoyed the turn-based, strategic combat of Baldur's Gate 3, or even Clair Obscur from last year. If you're a Star Wars fan, this is a no-brainer at this price, and one you'll likely enjoy the narrative of.

Okay, I've been focusing a fair bit on hardware, so let's shake things up and I'll recommend some PS5 game deals for a bit. Wait here, I'll go look over that hill, and come back with some cheaper games you can buy thanks to Black Friday.

I'm aware the Fractal Scape might be a bit of an unexpected headset recommendation, so allow me to justify it to you a little.

A lot of gaming headsets are very overt - you know from looking at them that they're for gaming, and they appeal to that with their designs. The Fractal Scape takes more of an Apple-esque approach? It's got a very clean-cut look and feel, with ample cushioning, and even though it actually has RGB lighting, it's used to enhance that classy feel instead of appealing to the mass market. It's built with premium materials and sits really comfortably on your head.

More importantly, it has really excellent audio quality for a mid-range headset, which I'd argue outclasses the SteelSeries Arctis Nova 7 I also have in my setup. It's not got the same simultaneous Bluetooth and 2.4GHz connectivity, which is a shame, but you can hot-swap back and forth between both modes. It comes with a fancy charging stand which I really like, and if I had to say it was missing one thing, it'd be a 3.5mm connection for wired use.

Read more of my thoughts on the Fractal Scape from when it took its first discount

In the lead-up to Black Friday, PlayStation sold all of its XR patents to Meta, and stock has been dwindling or removed entirely from some storefronts. It hasn't been confirmed, but PSVR 2 seems to have been quietly discontinued, so you may struggle to find it this Black Friday, let alone for a discounted price. I'll be looking for it, so stay tuned.

If you want to read more of my thoughts on the matter as a massive VR lover, I recently vented some in the piece linked below.

It's still not the easiest to find, but PS5 stock hasn't taken quite the same hit in the US as it has in the UK. You can get refurbished models at PlayStation Direct, but there are also options at Best Buy and other retailers.

As I find some fun bundles from different retailers, I'll shout them out here, so stay tuned.

Check out refurbished PS5 consoles at PlayStation Direct

It's getting to the time of day when US readers and shoppers are probably starting to wake up and smell the PS5 deals. If you're newly joining us, welcome, and feel free to peruse the deals I've highlighted so far. I've been concentrating on UK discounts so far, but I've supplied US links to equivalents in your region. From here on in, I'll probably start to look at US deals mainly, but I'll supply links for both territories so everyone's catered to!

Being able to add NVMe M.2 SSDs to the PS5 is honestly one of the console's best features.

Unfortunately, thanks to AI companies swallowing up the earth's supply of RAM and NAND tech, SSDs have become so, so, so much more expensive this year.

When I was reviewing SSDs regularly, 1TB drives were costing around $70, which was incredible. Now, you'd be lucky to find one for under $150, and that's without a heatsink on top.

SSD prices are actually ludicrous at the moment, to the point where honestly, I wouldn't recommend upgrading at all. This technology just shouldn't cost as much as it does, so I'd argue waiting to see if prices decrease is the better option, unless you really, really need more storage space and it's an emergency.

I'll be keeping an eye out for PS5 SSD deals and updating you if I find any I'd actually think are worth buying, but if you're wondering why there isn't a lot of SSD content on this live report, that'll be why.

Razer is also coming out swinging with its Black Friday PS5 deals. The Razer Raiju V3 Pro is one of the newest and best PS5 controllers money can buy, but it's also one of the most expensive, which is why I'm slightly surprised to see it discounted down to the same price as the older Nacon R5P I showed you a bit earlier on.

My guess is that with the DualSense Edge discounted, all the other brands are trying to compete.

Here, you get TMR thumbsticks that are symmetrical (which doesn't happen often in pro controller land), and six extra buttons. The whole thing is built with super responsive, clicky buttons, and there's a carry case, swappable thumbstick tops, and blanks if you don't want the back buttons being pressed accidentally.

What are you missing? The same as with any licensed third-party controller for PS5. You won't get haptic feedback or any vibration at all. I know, I know, that sucks compared to the DualSense, but direct your hate at Sony, not the controller brands who are just playing by the rules.

From what I can see, the entire range of SteelSeries Arctis Nova headsets is seeing discounts thanks to Black Friday PS5 deals. Depending on who you talk to, you'll hear different recommendations as to which of these headsets is the best to buy. There's a pretty big family of them, from the Nova 5, 7, Pro, Omni, and all of them have versions for different platforms and colorways, offering different selections of perks and features for your money.

Personally, I'd recommend the Nova 7 Gen 2. Its big selling point is that it has simultaneous Bluetooth and 2.4GHz connectivity, alongside the usual Arctis Nova perks. It's the mid-ranger that often goes unnoticed underneath the more "pro" models at the top of the price range, but a bit hard to justify above the value-led Arctis Nova 5.

Right now, you can get this headset in big Black Friday deals. The Black model is £129 at Amazon, and the beautiful Magenta version is even more affordable at £108. If you're not convinced by the classy Fractal Refine I've pointed out already, this is an alternative I'd point you toward if you want good value for money this week.

SteelSeries Arctis Nova 7 Gen 2: £129.99 at Amazon

Read more: SteelSeries Arctis Nova 7 Gen 2 review

If you're not satisfied with the first-party games from 2026, I don't know if you know this, but there's been a small, previously unheard-of indie game that seems to be getting a lot of praise right now called Grand Theft Auto 6, and somehow, you can already get it cheaper in the UK.

In all seriousness, if you're yet to jump into GTA 6, I think Amazon realised earlier this week that most people see no point in buying a code in a box and they're just buying the game digitally instead. Somehow, the biggest gaming launch of the decade saw a discount in its first week of launch.

Annoyingly, that deal, which brought GTA 6 down to £64, is now gone, but you can still get a clever workaround. If you do want to just buy it on the PlayStation Store, ShopTo is selling a £70 PSN voucher for £60, which means you can get GTA 6 even cheaper.

Okay, here's the first discounted PS5 accessory I want to throw a spotlight on.

I'm a controller reviewer, so I've tested all of the officially licensed pro controllers for PS5. My favorite one is a brand new one called the Nacon Revolution 5 Unlimited, but since it launched mere months ago, it's still hard to get a hold of, and it's not going to see a discount for Black Friday.

But wait, because Nacon has a slightly older trick up its sleeve. I noticed the slightly older, but still great Nacon Revolution 5 Pro discounted in the US, and its deal in the UK is even better.

The R5P was one of the first PS5 controllers with Hall effect sticks, meaning they won't bother you with stick drift issues. It also has four back buttons and a carry case full of accessories you can use to make it your own. Is the newer R5U better? Yes, without a doubt, you're missing out on TMR sticks, two additional bumper buttons, and sublime microswitch buttons. But the R5P is still excellent, and a great way to get more buttons than the DualSense Edge for less money.

Nacon Revolution 5 Pro: £129.99 at Amazon

Those deals will then last into Tuesday.

Personally, I'd beat the chance of deals disappearing or stock running out and shop sooner. At this point, you're almost certainly not going to see things get cheaper as the sale continues.

#3887. Mondrayn is a putrid, crunchy pixel art RPG about escaping from limbo where "dying doesn't mean the end of your suffering"

Everything's a bit grim these days, so let's just go all in on the misery shall we? Let's start with this line from the game's Steam page we'll be talking about today: "Mondrayn is a grim JRPG with survival elements where dying doesn't mean the end of your suffering." Crikey! You're telling me the sweet release of death won't be so saccharine after all? Sounds rough, so it's a good thing Mondrayn looks so darn compelling.

The world of Mondrayn is a dead one. You start out waking up in a city, it's in a gnarly state, of course, overrun by a disease of unknown origin. Horrible monsters are roaming about the place, cults are performing nasty rituals, and you've got no memories, so all you can do is try and make any friends you can, kill the undead and get out of, all places, limbo.

Mondrayn is an RPG in the sense that it utilises turn-based combat, "intertwined with shootouts." I'm not entirely sure how that manifests, you do seem to be able to do both regular attacks and special moves, the state of characters seems to have an impact, but truthfully I don't mind not understanding because what I'm here for are the utterly, delectably rancid vibes on display.

Every single pixel in this game looks like it was dipped in a vat of grime, puss, blood and vomit, and I revel in it! The enemy portraits are crunchy and violet, they look ripped straight out of some obscure art book for a Warhammer-esque tabletop game no one has ever heard of. It looks a bit fantasy, a bit steampunk, and incredibly, incredibly grimdark. It's the kind of world I'd rather instantly top myself than spend a second longer in, so, kudos to the fictional characters in it that have no choice in the matter for managing better than me. As it stands, Mondrayn has no release date, but you can wishlist it on Steam in the meantime.

#3886. The siren call of user-generated content has caught Dead by Daylight in its snare, as Behaviour Interactive outline a big revamp update slated for next year

Weather, new models, better maps, it'll have it all

The promise of user-generated content, this idea that you could host a platform that grows infinitely because the people that interact with it make things for it and you don't even have to pay anyone, is an alluring one. And its siren call has come for Dead by Daylight, as developer Behaviour Interactive have outlined the future of the game, which includes a way to make your own bits for the multiplayer horror game.

"What if you could create your own Dead by Daylight experiences?" explains a blog post recapping the plans for how the game is going to change. "As one of the most exciting updates coming in 2027, the Dead by Daylight Workshop will open the doors to user-created content in some incredible ways. From designing your own Maps and importing custom assets, to modifying game rules, objectives, and even creating entirely new modes, the possibilities are vast."

The post goes on to note that anything created in the workshop will "exist separately from all our classic modes, with dedicated creation tools and moderation provided to ensure experienced modders have everything they need to do their best work, and all submissions meet our official guidelines." I am always hesitant when it comes to UGC faff, because the ability to make your own custom Debbie Daylight maps might sound promising, but people do actually have to engage with them for the whole thing to work. It's just putting a hat on a hat!

Anyway, the workshop isn't the only thing Behaviour have in the works. For one, the game is getting a big visual overhaul. You can expect lighting improvements, more detailed assets and "tons of atmospheric touches," alongside revamps of particular maps like the Temple of Purgation and Backwater Swamp. Killers and survivors will be getting some TLC too by "improving character textures, proportions, hair, and animations to make them look and feel more lifelike. That includes updated character rigs, new motion capture, and new facial animation technology designed to better express a character’s fear, pain, and struggles over the course of a Trial."

Beyond all of that, a dynamic weather system is coming to the game, meaning you'll now have to deal with the likes of rain, thunderstorms, snow and heavy wind, all of which can impact matches. Onboarding for newer folks should be getting some improvements too, with the addition of a "more cinematic introduction, clearer explanations and tutorials of game mechanics, and a more gradual introduction," to the game. All of this will be coming in one big update sometime in 2027, so, keep your eyes peeled for whenever that drops.

#3885. The Wolf Among Us Remastered for Switch launches November 29

The Switch version of The Wolf Among Us Remastered will launch via Nintendo eShop on November 29 for $24.99, Telltale Games announced.

While originally scheduled to launch on October 29 alongside the PlayStation 5, Xbox Series, Xbox One, and PC (Steam, Epic Games Store) versions, the Switch version was delayed for further quality improvements.

Here is an overview of the game, via Telltale Games:

Fairy tales are real. Murder is just the beginning.

Step back into Fabletown in The Wolf Among Us Remastered—the definitive edition of Telltale’s acclaimed noir narrative thriller inspired by DC’s award-winning Fables comic series.

Critically acclaimed, The Wolf Among Us became one of the most celebrated story-driven adventures of its generation, praised for its unforgettable characters, sharp writing, and meaningful player choice.

Fully remastered with enhanced visuals and modern presentation, this definitive edition brings Bigby Wolf’s first investigation to life with greater atmosphere, immersion, and detail than ever before – honoring the original experience while introducing Fabletown to a new generation of players.

Investigate brutal murders, interrogate suspects, explore crime scenes, and uncover a conspiracy hiding beneath the streets of Fabletown, where myths and legends live secretly among us.

Every choice carries consequences. In Fabletown, justice isn’t clean, and sometimes the Big Bad Wolf is the only one willing to do what must be done.

New Avengers: Doomsday international teaser shows Thor and Steve Rogers visiting Castle Doom after the villain drops the coldest line yet

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Just one day after Marvel dropped the final trailer, a new international teaser for Avengers: Doomsday has arrived, giving us another look at Robert Downey Jr.'s villain.

The teaser, which was originally shared by Disney Korea but has since been posted on Twitter by ScreenRant, opens with Doctor Doom delivering his coldest line yet. "You call yourselves heroes? Avengers, Fantastic Four, X-Men? You shall all kneel before Doom." The rest of the clip contains shots of Marvel heroes Johnny Storm, Thing, and Thor showing off their powers, before the Fantastic Four, the Wakandans, and Shang-Chi meet up in what looks like Steve Rogers' retro house. Watch the full video below.

The Disney Korea account has shared a new Avengers: Doomsday international trailer! Watch Here 👇 https://t.co/nZ9grAnKkdNovember 24, 2026

However, the most interesting part comes right at the end, where we see Thor and Steve Rogers visit Doom Castle, where Doctor Doom sits on the throne. What could the duo be doing walking right into the villain's lair? This seemingly supports the fan theory that Doom may be pretending to be an ally to the Avengers early on in the film.

More evidence arrived in the new Doomsday trailer, where fans pointed out that someone seems to be edited out of the Fantastic Four lineup when the group goes to visit Steve Rogers at his house. We already know that Doom has been collecting Marvel heroes ahead of Doomsday, starting with kidnapping Hulk during the Endgame Encore added footage. Also, during the VisionQuest finale, we learn that Doom has already resurrected Scarlett Witch, and seemingly made her one of his Latverian Witches.

So, could Doom be pouring poison into Rogers' and Thor's ears? Alas, the new scene could just be the pair visiting the villain to try and reason with him, as we can guess from the synopsis, the baddie is set to do a lot of damage in the new movie. There is also the issue of Steve Rogers flipping between timelines. We know that Doom has a personal vendetta against the Avengers due to the multiversal damage they caused at the end of Avengers: Endgame when Steve went back in time to be with Peggy after returning the Infinity Stones. Perhaps Steve is visiting Doom Castle to make amends.

All will be revealed when Avengers: Doomsday hits cinemas on December 18, and December 16 in the UK. For more, check out our guide to the Marvel timeline, and keep up with upcoming Marvel movies and shows on the way.

#3883. Slow down a bit and help a cow find a friend in the lush-looking, hand-drawn, milk deliver-em-up Milki Delivery, which is out now

I don't want to write about video games any more, I want to deliver milk in the countryside and hang out with a cow and quirky people! Sorry, what, there's a game all about that called Milki Delivery that came out today? Alright, I'll write about video games again, especially when they look as charming as this one does.

The stakes at play in Milki Delivery are very low (as are the steaks, no butchery to be found here, only one very sweet looking cow I couldn't possibly slaughter). You play as Neha, and she's made a promise to her pet cow, the titular Milki, that you'll find her a friend (I think this is a world where there aren't any cows left; yikes!). To do that, all you have to do is deliver her milk! Accept because this is an adventure game, you'll have to help out a few folks along the way.

It's a game very much about the journey, as when riding about this lush and bright countryside, you might find a group of cats that just need a little taste of that sweet creamy juice you've got. Or maybe you have some rope that a farmer needs to wrassle up some sheep. Sometimes you'll have to get a bit more involved with the various people you meet, but predominantly, you'll be delivering milk to folks who need it.

Getting around the place is quite simple too, you plot out your path ahead of time and let the game take you as it's all mouse driven. A relaxed experience to be sure, but the game's art is just so delightful to look at, I'm quite enticed by the idea of just slowing down and enjoying some pretty pictures and making friends along the way. You can make different kinds of milk, too, just be feeding Milki different ingredients. Not how that works in real life, but now I kind of wish it was.

In any case, Milki Delivery is out now, and you can pick it up on Steam.

Repair the Reynolds Kit Car by finding some wrecks.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The GTA 6 Kit Car locations are spread all over Leonida, making your search to repair Wyman's fourth car significantly more involved than the Transgressor, Riata, or even the Mamba GT. There are five whole cars to scan with the WAiNK It app, but it's well worth it, because the Kit Car is super fast and stylish.

It's worth noting that you'll need to complete the Chapter 3 mission, Meet the Heders, to acquire the cut-off tool (since one of the Kit Cars is in a locked shipping container). After the Kit Car, there's one additional vehicle in the Classic Car Collection, the Deviant, but it doesn't actually require a collectible hunt as Wyman will simply offer it to you, making this your last one.

The first Kit Car is inside the garage at Willie's Service Center in south Vice City, southeast of Salton, and northwest of Tequesta. Just north of the purchasable 7th Avenue Garage and west of Vice City Firearms,you'll spot a building on the left labelled as Willie's Service Center with a brown top half and blue lower half.

Enter the ground floor via the door around the left side by the stairs. You'll have to break in, which sounds an alarm, so be quick scanning the car inside.

The second one is on Casanova Island, the rightmost of the Rialto Islands that connect west Vice City with east Vice City. When you reach the island, driving west to east (coming from Vespucci) head along the northernmost road and look to your left about halfway across the island for a big white villa with a small gated garage next door—it's next to a big vacant lot. Push the gate open to find the kit car right in front of you.

The third one is in a shipping container on Wild Hog Point, directly to the southwest of Port Gellhorn, on the big peninsula that sticks out where the airfield is located. For this one, you'll need to have completed the Meet the Heders mission in Chapter 3 to acquire the cut-off tool to open it.

It's on the westernmost edge of the point, around the middle of the pools that look a bit like a seahorse on the map. Due to the end of Chapter 2, similar to Grassrivers, this area is also a hot spot for police, so be careful while driving around. Look for the yellow scoop container, crack it open, and scan the car inside.

The fourth one is around the back of Donnie's Auto Repair Watson Bay in Watson Bay town, west of Hamlet, southwest of Port Gellhorn. This garage (which has Donnie's Auto Repair written on it) is next door to the Pay 'n' Spray - Watson Bay. Just head around the left side of the building and you'll find the Kit Car to scan immediately on your right.

The fifth Kit Car is in a fancy garage on the west side of Capri on the little curving northern peninsula of houses. Capri is south of Port Gellhorn on the coast. Drive along the road until you spot the building site on your right and the green villa on your left—just after it, you'll find the driveway of the house you want, also on the left. Follow the path and break into the garage on your right to find the car.

Same as always, wait for Wyman to finish the car and call, then click the payment request he sends in his following text to Buck him $1,500 before collecting the car from the nav point at his scrapyard.

This is actually the final car hunt, as later Wyman will call you and straight-up ask if you want the final car, a Deviant. You then pay him $1,000 for labour, and it's immediately yours to collect, so with this, you've basically finished the Classic Car Collection.

Capcom has announced that its dinosaur shooter Exoprimal will be unplayable next September as the servers are being taken offline.

While not quite as massive as the year it had in 2026, Capcom's 2023 was incredible, with Resident Evil 4 and Street Fighter 6 releasing as two certified game of the year contenders and as two of the all-time greats in their respective genres. But there was another, namely Exoprimal, a PvPvE shooter where you took a ton of Overwatch-like character classes into brawls where you'd fend off armies of dinosaurs.

It had a bit of a cult following, but Capcom has announced it'll be joining the pile of dead live service titles next year. In a post on the Exoprimal website, Capcom confirms that services for the game will go offline on September 29, 2027, with the post reading, "We cannot thank you enough for the love and support you have shown over the years, and we sincerely apologize for the gravity of this announcement."

As it begins the shutdown process, the game's survival pass premium tiers (aka, the paid battle pass) have been removed from the in-game store already. The game itself will be taken off sale on March 30, 2027, and those who own it will have six more months to play it before it's gone forever. With no way to access the content in single-player, it'll sadly join the ever-growing list of games that are just gone, which certainly isn't a bad omen for the all-digital future.

Exoprimal was perhaps best known for being the bane of many a Dino Crisis fan upon its announcement – especially when there's a character who looks like that game's heroine Regina, who featured heavily in marketing. It was genuinely a fun time when you got into it, but it suffered from the same fate many live services do, that being there's too damn many of them, so it never really took off. It also didn't help that Exoprimal's best content was hidden behind a ton of playtime.

Dino Crisis is more than "Resident Evil with dinosaurs" – it shaped survival horror as we know it.

#3879. Sci-fi RPG Exodus continues evoking Mass Effect by revealing female lead and nicknaming her FemJun

Sci-fi role-playing game Exodus continues to play into the Mass Effect comparisons by revealing the female version of its main character Jun, and with studio Archetype referring to her in marketing material as FemJun.

If that moniker sounds familiar it's because it is: the female Commander Shepard character in the Mass Effect series was nicknamed FemShep. FemShep became an iconic part of BioWare's iconic series, eventually proving that female leads could front games just as successfully as male leads could, and be every bit as popular.

Is the nickname FemJun too blatant? Possibly. But there's well publicised BioWare pedigree at Archetype Entertainment, in the studio's co-founders and in the people leading the project. Key Mass Effect writer Drew Karpyshyn is in charge of writing Exodus, for example, and the similarities to Mass Effect are something the Exodus team has not been shy about in the past. In the wake of Mass Effect 5 being cancelled and BioWare being closed, they become even more alluring.

There are, however, big and important differences between Exodus and Mass Effect, key among them, time dilation. In Exodus, there are special Exodus missions whereby you leave your home planet and fly far away, and in doing so experience time differently to the people back home. Many years will pass for them while only days will pass for you, which provides the game with a way to show you long-term consequences of your actions when you return.

Archetype hasn't shown the female version of Jun before, despite having released many videos of Exodus, perhaps to build anticipation for her reveal. It's a press beat that's also provided Archetype - a studio owned by Dungeons & Dragons company Wizards of the Coast - with an occasion to reveal the two actors playing Jun in the game.

Female Jun is portrayed by Carina Conti, who played the lead in the recent Mafia game, The Old Country - Isabella Torrisi. She's appeared in HBO's Winning Time and Hulu/Freeform's Good Trouble as well. Male Jun, meanwhile, is portrayed by Stephen Oyoung, who played Mister Negative in Insomniac's Marvel's Spider-Man 1 and 2 games, and Red Hood in Gotham Knights. He also appeared in Mission: Impossible - The Final Reckoning, The Wrecking Crew, and Twisters. The game also famously stars Matthew McConaughey.

Archetype announced a Dark Horse hardback art book to go on sale alongside the game next year as well. This arrives a week after the game; Exodus arrives 7th April 2027 on PC, PS5 and Xbox Series S/X, and the art book on 13th April.

Matt played Exodus at Gamescom relatively recently and came away impressed, referring to it as "the best kind of surprise". "I wasn't expecting quite such a bombastic 45 minutes when I first picked up a controller and settled into Exodus, admittedly, but the more I played, the more it made sense," he wrote. "I might not be much of a Mass Effect fan (damn you M35 Mako once more), but Exodus is now firmly on my radar ahead of its arrival next year."
